problem: LLM-based VLN agents (NavGPT, MapGPT, TINA) rely on a fixed LLM knowledge base and treat past trajectories only as a replay buffer for the current episode. They cannot distill reusable knowledge across tasks, so they do not improve with experience.
motivation: Natural agents refine navigation skill through repeated journeys, whereas current VLN agents evolve only through manual tuning or model retraining. A training-free agent that stores, retrieves and corrects its own experience at test time could keep improving without large-scale annotated data.
key_idea: A training-free MLLM navigation agent combines a verbal topological map plus a Chroma experience repository, RAG+CoT multi-step decisions, and a reflection module that uses simulator outcome scores to correct the first bad decision and write it back as reusable experience.
insight: Gains come from the combination of CoT, reflection and experience. Without CoT, reflection adds only +3.0 SR (34.4→37.4), while with CoT it adds +8.4 SR (46.3→54.7), because CoT traces give reflection something to correct. Ground-truth outcome scores are needed, since LLMs cannot reliably find their own errors (outcome evaluator ablation, Fig.3). More experience helps but saturates: 2-shot beats 5-shot, and gains flatten from 0 to 50 stored experiences, as context dilution and homogeneous experience limit further benefit.
method: Verbal topological map: short-term memory, a dynamic graph G_t whose nodes are annotated with MLLM text descriptions of observations and the think/plan/execute decision record.
Experience repository: long-term memory in Chroma vector DB; each entry is a quadruple of landmark features, scene descriptions, original decision (T,P,A) and corrected decision (T',P',A').
Experience retriever: an MLLM extracts landmarks from the instruction, SBERT (768-d) encodes them, and cosine similarity returns the top-N (best N=2) experiences as few-shot examples.
Prompt generator: builds the per-step prompt from the task description, the instruction, the encoded map memory and the retrieved few-shot experience.
Multi-step decider: CoT MLLM outputs thinking, planning and executing at each step, and the trace is saved back into the map.
Outcome evaluator: after each episode, computes NE/SR/SPL/OSR from simulator ground truth (human feedback in the real world).
Experience corrector: an MLLM reads the map memory and the scores, finds the first unreasonable decision, writes the corrected decision, and adds the new experience to the repository.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen, main); also tested Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini-2.0-Pro, Qwen2-VL, InternVL2.5; SBERT for retrieval
setting.training_data: none (training-free); experience accumulated at test time from prior episodes with GT-based reflection
setting.observation: panoramic RGB views of navigable viewpoints converted to text descriptions by the MLLM
setting.privileged: Ground-truth trajectory and simulator metrics (NE/SR/SPL/OSR) are used by the outcome evaluator for reflection, and experience is accumulated over test episodes

results: SE-VLN (GPT-4o) reaches SR 54.7 on the 72-scene R2R subset versus MapGPT GPT-4o at 46.3, and SR 57 versus 46 on the R2R val-unseen table. On REVERIE val-unseen it gets SR 35.2 versus MapGPT's 30.6. It is still far below supervised methods such as DUET (SR 72 on R2R) and ScaleVLN (81).
limitations: Depends on ground-truth simulator outcomes for reflection; in the real world it would need human feedback.
Self-evolution flattens with more experience, and more shots (5) hurt because of context dilution.
Gap to supervised SOTA remains large; evaluated on subsets, with a different scene count in Table 3, and cost/latency of multiple GPT-4o calls is not discussed.
